clue.text: Maybe cook's run through chaotic beer tent outside old church

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go round the other pieces
chaotic signals that the letters of beer tent are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook bustles through a disorderly beer tent at a fete, skirting the old church nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' makes ENBRETTE from BEER TENT, and 'outside' puts it round O and CH. 'Maybe cook's' signals that the definition describes how a cook might prepare something.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked en brochette is threaded on a skewer, so a cook might well have run it through.

clue.text: Locally souse Greek character in English beer

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dialect instruction to drench a Greek in English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect sense: to souse can mean to strike someone, and earhole as a verb means to box someone's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: In regional English, souse means to hit or cuff, matching a dialect verb for clipping someone round the ear.

clue.text: Radical German engineer, outwardly youthful

parts.note: Karl Benz was the German engineer behind the motor car

indicators.note: outwardly asks only for the outside letters of youthful, its first and last

explanation.surface: A revolutionary German engineer who still looks young on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' is the chemistry sense, a group of atoms acting as a unit, not a political firebrand.
explanation.definitionFit: Benzyl is a chemical radical, a group of atoms derived from toluene that behaves as a unit.

clue.text: Stout deliveries with crew

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so a run of deliveries
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A brewery's dark beer goes out on delivery rounds with a team of draymen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer but is the adjective; 'deliveries' is cricket bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes a heavily built, plump person, which is what being overweight amounts to.

clue.text: Cut roof off of shelter

indicators.note: in a down entry the roof is the top letter, so taking the roof off drops the first letter

parts.note: a shack is a rough hut serving as a shelter

explanation.surface: Instructions for chopping the roof off a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to chop roughly, as with an axe, so it is a synonym of cut.

clue.text: Girl, thin, picked up fabric

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: Terry can be a girl's name and lean means thin

explanation.surface: A slim girl lifts up a piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRY LEAN, said aloud, gives the fabric's name. 'Girl' is TERRY, often spelt Terri for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Terylene is a British trade name for a polyester fibre used in clothing material.

clue.text: Needs, say, barriers, without using force

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does

indicators.note: without using says the letter for force is dropped from the barriers

parts.note: fences are barriers
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Requirements, such as fences, put up without any force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without using' drops F from FENCES. Egence is a rare word for a need.
explanation.definitionFit: Egences is a rare word for wants or necessities, the plural of egence, a pressing requirement.

clue.text: Choke left out — that's odd

indicators.note: out says the letter for left leaves the word

parts.note: to strangle is to choke

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the choke has been left out of a car and finds it peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and odd are synonyms, both meaning unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: Test cheese crackers, including note to describe background

indicators.note: including says the scrambled letters take in the note
crackers means crazy, so the letters of test cheese are scrambled

explanation.surface: Try cheese on crackers while taking a note, to give the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits for the cheese but means mad. 'including' puts N inside the jumble of TEST CHEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the scene is to give the context or background before a story begins.

clue.text: Critics having face-off in secret places

indicators.note: having the face off means the front letter is taken away

parts.note: scorners are those who scorn, scathing critics

explanation.surface: Critics confront each other in hidden spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-off' suggests a confrontation, but it means removing the face, the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Corners can be secluded, out-of-the-way spots, as in remote corners of the earth.

clue.text: Environmentally friendly sunbelt Asia developed

indicators.note: developed means grown or changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Green policies in a developing sunny part of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustainable practices can continue without depleting resources, which is what environmentally friendly means.

clue.text: How 22 might be seen in braces

definitions.text: How 22 might be seen in braces

parts.words: How 22 might be seen in braces
parts.note: the digits 2 and 2 are a two and a two; braces are pairs, so seen in braces means taken in pairs

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a number would look printed on a pair of trouser braces.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' is not a cross-reference but two twos; a brace is a pair, so in braces means in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals entering the ark went in pairs, the phrase used for anything arranged in couples.

clue.text: Masses of badgers changing hands

indicators.note: changing hands means right is swapped for left, R for L

parts.note: brock is an old British name for a badger

explanation.surface: Large numbers of badgers pass to new owners.
explanation.definitionFit: Blocks are large solid masses, as of stone or ice.

clue.text: Give gun to old Mafia boss for final conflict

parts.note: to arm someone is to give them a weapon
aged means old
a don is a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: Handing a weapon to an elderly gangster before the last showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Armageddon is the site of the last battle between good and evil.

clue.text: Lean despicable character

definitions.meaning: a ship ... when it leans over to one side

explanation.surface: A thin, contemptible villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Heel means both to tilt over, as a yacht does, and a scoundrel.

clue.text: Nice Maoris represented Pacific region

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Friendly Maori people stood for an area of the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is the group of small islands in the western Pacific Ocean, north of Melanesia.

clue.text: Heavenly present recently sent back for wrapping

indicators.note: for wrapping says the reversed word goes round the other piece
in a down entry sent back means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: late can mean recently, as in of late
here means present, as at a roll-call

explanation.surface: A divine gift was lately returned to be gift-wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means here, at hand; 'sent back' reverses the word for recently, giving ETAL, and 'for wrapping' puts it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something airy and otherworldly, belonging to the heavens.

clue.text: In which to note cash and stuff?

parts.note: scratch is slang for money
to pad is to stuff or fill out

explanation.surface: Where should one record one's money and possessions?
explanation.definitionFit: A scratchpad is a pad of paper for jotting quick notes.

clue.text: Independent daily newspaper held up by gross, mean American

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: rank means gross or offensive

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British daily

explanation.surface: A newspaper delayed by a disgusting, stingy American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the paper's letters to TFI, which 'held' puts inside. 'mean American' is a noun phrase: a nasty person, in US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratfink is American slang for a contemptible person or informer, someone mean.

clue.text: Symbol of lawless vocabulary

indicators.note: lawless splits as law-less: the Latin word for law is taken away from the vocabulary

parts.note: a lexicon is a vocabulary or word list

explanation.surface: A sign of an unruly way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lawless' reads as 'law' removed: LEX is the Latin for law, so it leaves LEXICON.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or emblem that stands for something, a symbol.

clue.text: Spicy little number caught on the level, mostly

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: the horizon is the level line where earth meets sky

explanation.surface: A saucy little song or dance turns out to be honest after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little number' suggests a song or outfit but is a dish on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a spicy Spanish pork sausage, a small item one might order.

clue.text: Arabic poem in question, suppressed words briefly preceding answer

indicators.note: preceding says the shortened aside comes before the answer letter
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an aside is words spoken under one's breath, suppressed

explanation.surface: A query about an Arab poem, with some muttered words given before the reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A qasida is a classical Arabic or Persian ode, often of praise or elegy.

clue.text: One in three, alternatively one of two

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
alternatively here means in another arrangement, so the letters of three are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle in counting: one out of three, or one out of two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternatively' looks like a link to the definition but rearranges THREE as ETHER, with I placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Either refers to one or the other of a pair, any one of two things.

clue.text: That man about to introduce grave sacrifice

parts.note: he means that man
ca, short for circa, means about
a tomb is a grave

explanation.surface: He is about to bring in a serious offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like an adjective for the sacrifice but is TOMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was a great public sacrifice in ancient Greece, originally of a hundred oxen.

clue.text: India satisfied over point

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: met as in met a demand, satisfied it

explanation.surface: India is content after a matter is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a separate point on a list or agenda.

clue.text: Pressing information interrupts departure

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an exit is a departure
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Urgent news breaks in on someone's leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means demanding urgent attention, which is what pressing means.

clue.text: Opt to keep current dispatch for Mars, say

indicators.note: to keep says the opting word holds the current inside it

parts.note: to opt is to decide
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Choosing to keep the electricity running for a mission to the red planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' is the Roman god of war, not the planet: deicide is killing a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Deicide means the killing of a god, and Mars is an example of a god.

clue.text: Peak weight restricting single bloke having drink

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the weight goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a kilo is a weight
I is the Roman numeral for one, single
a bloke is a man
a jar is British slang for a drink, especially of beer

explanation.surface: A heavy single man restricted to one drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa, a famous peak in Tanzania.
